precepts.text: The children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim: little images we made of family members. Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king, and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days. So in these latter days, David's going to be here. Who he is, we don't know.
precepts.point: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
Amos says the tabernacle of David is fallen. Hosea tells how long it lies fallen: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim.” Teraphim are the little images we made of family members. Many days with none of it: no king, no prince, no priesthood.

“Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

So in these latter days, David is going to be here. Who he is, we don't know. But the children of Israel who have gone so long without a king will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king, and that is the tabernacle of David raised up and built as in the days of old.

precepts.text: How long shall it be to the end of these wonders? A time, times, and an half: a time is a hundred years, times is two hundred, and an half: 350 years, and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people. Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed: we forgot who we are, we even forgot our nationality. After 70 AD our country was destroyed, but we still built cities in Africa, still had kings and governments, still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power was scattered.
precepts.point: Without the ephod: no priest there to guide you and tell you what God needs you to do. That's the religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance stripped away.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
Hosea says the children of Israel “shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod”. Daniel 12 gives the time frame for it. “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?” The wonders are our people being destroyed, enslaved and colonized, being without a king, without a prince, without an ephod.

“it shall be for a time, times, and an half”. A time is a hundred years; times is two hundred, three hundred in all; and an half makes 350 years. “and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.” Within those 350 years we were totally destroyed. All that power was gone from us; we forgot who we are, and we even forgot our nationality.

When we fled Jerusalem in 70 AD, was our power destroyed? Our country was destroyed, but we went to Africa and built cities there, and the ten tribes were set up on this side of the world doing their thing too. We still had governments, we still had kings over us, and we still knew we were the children of Israel. It was within the slave trade and colonization that the power of the holy people was scattered.

That is the many days without a king: without political sovereignty, when Europe colonized Ghana, Nigeria, Angola, Senegal, Papua New Guinea and the Congo, and when the transatlantic slave trade took us. It is without an image: our minds destroyed until the sisters in Africa bleach their skin and put on weaves, because worshipping the God of your oppressor destroys the way you look at yourself. The same curses fell on our people all over Africa, like the Mau Mau in Kenya, tortured in British camps and paid less than 4,000 pounds each. That is why I don't want no damn reparations.

precepts.text: From the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up.
precepts.point: Without the ephod: no priest there to guide you and tell you what God needs you to do. That's the religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance stripped away.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
Daniel 12 gives the time frame for when our people would be without a king, without an image, and without a sacrifice, as Hosea 3:4 says. Verse 11 reads: “And from the time that the daily sacrifice shall be taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.”

The daily sacrifice taken away is Hosea's “without a sacrifice”. Without the sacrifice, the image and the ephod, all our religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance was stripped away, and there was no priest to guide us and tell us what God needs us to do. The white man came in, whipped us, taught us white Jesus and his lies, and forced it down our throats in Africa. After he brought the slaves over here, he went to Africa and destroyed them there, until the people in Africa don't even know that we in the Caribbean and America are the same people.

So from the taking away of the sacrifice, the days are counted, and the question Daniel asked, “How long shall it be to the end of these wonders?”, is answered with a set time. That goes back to the yoke of iron upon thy neck until thou have been destroyed: it did not just happen to us over here, it happened to our people in Africa, and the scattering of the holy people runs its appointed course.

precepts.text: Israel abides many days without a king, a prince or a sacrifice; afterward they return and seek the Lord their God and David their king.
precepts.point: Fear thou not, O my servant Jacob: what he says will happen makes us afraid, so we increase our faith by remembering this body is a shell. I will save thee from afar and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and none shall make him afraid. Though I make a full end of all nations, the extras born in vain with Esau the villain, I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure and not leave thee altogether unpunished.
precepts.why:
“In that day”, “I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him”: that's Christ's return. “But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” Uh-oh. Did you notice? David is alive.

Hosea says the same: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim”. Many days without a king. “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.”

We are returning now. We are seeking the Lord our God. And it is telling you David is going to be alive in these last days, in the latter days, when Israel returns. That is the day of Jeremiah 30, when the yoke is broken off our neck and the Lord raises David up unto us.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

precepts.why:
“If ye transgress, I will scatter you abroad among the nations.” That was always the stipulation: if we transgress, God will scatter us among the nations.

“But if ye turn unto me, and keep my commandments, and do them; though there were of you cast out unto the uttermost part of the heaven, yet will I gather them from thence.” No matter how far our people are scattered, he is going to gather the Israelites, “and will bring them unto the place that I have chosen to set my name there”: back to Jerusalem, the place he chose. That is the return of Hosea 3:5.

note.label: Ashke-Nazis - Blow Up Gaza & New Jerusalem

precepts.why:
“For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king”: we have no king even today. “And without a prince”: we have no prince. “And without a sacrifice”: we have no sacrifice. “And without an image”: that’s the part I wanted. We have no image today; our image has been erased.

So when we talk about the Dark Ages, it’s only to show y’all our images. We only show the images of our people during the Dark Ages to show that we ruled, we were kings and leaders and warriors during that time, but we were not righteous. Remember it said all men that had life died off.

The book ‘Image of the Black in Western Art’, from Harvard; they won’t teach you this in school. St Maurice, a black man, showing that we were the knights of the time: these were the images they had throughout Europe of a black man and black men. St Maurice and his companions, all them black men. They make you think that during the Dark Ages we were nonexistent. No, we ruling; we pushed them white folks up into the caves of the Caucasus mountains. St Maurice was a military leader, legendary over the Theban legion of Rome during the 3rd century: St Maurice and his 6,000 African soldiers, black men. You’ll never see this on TV or in the movies; they’ll show you white folks everywhere. They were ordered to put down a rebellion against the empire, and when St Maurice discovered they were all Christians, he and his men refused to fight their fellow Christians and refused to sacrifice to the Roman god. That’s what got them put to death: the emperor killed St Maurice and all his legion because they didn’t follow his orders.

The earliest surviving work portraying Maurice as a dark complexioned African dates from the 12th century; now we know that he was an Israelite. Then the part I want y’all to see: the black images of him died out in the mid 16th century, undermined by the developing Atlantic slave trade. I wonder why. They didn’t want the slaves to know that we was warriors and saints and leaders. That’s what these damn devils did; that’s why they hide it in the books today. Once again the color black had become associated with spiritual darkness and otherness: he’s evil, he ain’t right. That’s what they did.

Another book: we worshipped Mary during the Dark Ages. She’s in the center of all these images. Icons from the Moscow Kremlin museums, from the 1550s, follow the text of the prayer chanted in honor of the Virgin: we were doing prayers and honoring Mary, the ever virgin, they called her. So this is not us reigning with Christ for a thousand years. These famous images of Mary and baby Christ we only show to show they were black, painted by black people; but this was a time of darkness. When I say darkness, I mean we did not have the truth; we was being wicked.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

points: For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image. So what we do as a people is we reach for the most tangible thing. And our women, they want to look just like Cesare Borgia's Christ. That is what they are trying to look like. That is why they do the blonde hair, the straight hair. They are trying to look like the closest thing to the great white hope that has been a false image and a narrative to our people.

Men, we are not really looking to look like that. We want to look like what is going to progress us the fastest way in life. And you know what that was in the eighties and the nineties? The pimps, the players, the drug dealers, the brothers with the flashy jewelry. They had the cars and the girls. So we attracted ourselves to that image until it became vibrant culture. I will say it like that. And now it is in our rap music. It is in our media. It is in our everyday flow of life. And we started to decline.

Shall abide many days without a king and without a prince. So without a king, it is talking about our kings. We would not have a nation or ruler. But to bring it up to speed to today, we do not have a leader. Anybody that we had as a leader was either assassinated, a false leader, or we saw that in the best of their abilities they led us in a wrong way, and we scatter and disperse. We have seen that in the Chronicles and the Kings, on how we had all these different kings and they chose their own way. They chose idolatry or different things outside of keeping the commandments.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: For the children of Israel shall abide many days: those many days are the roughly 350 years. Without a king and without a prince: we had no sovereignty; we were colonized and enslaved.
Without a sacrifice: no religious establishment teaching us true religion or teaching us about our God. In slavery the white man taught us his lies and his god.

And without an image: image goes into nationality, and into what your God looks like, because your God was created in your image. For many years we were without an image, without a sacrifice, without a culture. With culture you have your God and your nation, your feast days, how you worship: that is your heritage, and for many years we were without it.

The children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod. The king goes into political sovereignty: governing your country and ruling yourself. When were we without it? When Europe colonized us in Africa; before that we had kings. And when the transatlantic slave trade took us. They took Ghana, Nigeria, Angola, Senegal, Papua New Guinea, the Congo, and you had no sovereignty.

Without an image: our mind was destroyed in slavery and in colonialism. You go to Africa: the sisters bleach their skin and put on weaves. Where did that come from? Our image was destroyed. When you worship a God that does not look like you, it does something to your psyche; when you worship the God of your oppressor, it destroys the way you look at yourself.
Without the ephod: no priest there to guide you and tell you what God needs you to do. That's the religious infrastructure and spiritual guidance stripped away.

Video played in class: a history of British rule in Kenya and the Mau Mau uprising of 1952, one line for the record: the detention camps, the torture of detainees, the burned files rediscovered in 2011, and Britain's 2013 admission, paying 20 million pounds to 5,228 survivors, less than 4,000 pounds each, with not a single officer ever charged. That's why I tell y'all I don't want no damn reparations. You can do things like that to my people and then talk about you're holding this money right here?

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

points: Black Panther: they had a black cast, and the brother that wrote the movie is also a black man, which is beautiful, the representation that we need.

I want to focus on that word image. The children of Israel shall abide many days without an image. Why? Because we was sent into captivity as slaves for our disobedience to God's laws. Our culture was taken away from us, our nationality was taken away from us, our homeland was taken away, but more importantly our images were taken away from us.
What do we have now? We have the … of the so-called white man that's being portrayed to our people 24/7 by way of television and his so-called media.
There's a saying that we all would say, especially from Deacon …: image is everything.

When you look at these various televisions in society today they portray the black man as a drug dealer, adulterer, gangbanger and so forth. We have really no positive imagery going out for black men.

I would say about 95% of the movie was great. At the end of the movie there's something that Black Panther did which I disagreed on; however, as far as how our people are portrayed, in a nutshell I would have to say that the movie portrayed our people in a very positive light.

Let's get back to the Bible now. So listen good, black man, and you black women, you be quiet when you're speaking against your daddies, your brothers and sons; you don't know what happened to us. But this Bible is to cure all.
The children of Israel would abide many days: that's talking about slavery. Without a king, without a sacrifice, without an image. Why? Because our image was destroyed.

“For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice”: we were without leaders, without a prophet or priest of God to tell us what to do, because our kings went into slavery too. This is when we were taken from Spain, from Africa and from all these countries and brought here as slaves.

“And without an image”: for over 350 years we had no image and no identity; we lost our nationality. As Psalms 83 says, they said, let us cut them off from being a nation. What is seen today is a destroyed people; that is what the white man did to us in slavery.

“Afterward shall the children of Israel return”: that is happening now. As we return we get back our image, because we start understanding who we are, who our God is and what he looks like, and we start to claim our racial identity. “And seek the Lord their God, and David their king”: we are seeking the Lord our God, and that is what is being seen now.
In hitting the streets and teaching, what we are doing is making a movement toward repentance and change, reform and transformation.

“For the children of Israel shall abide many days”, centuries, “without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image”: we had no image. Our image was garbage. A Christian on YouTube said teaching black and brown children to love their skin color is racial idolatry, but teaching them the white man was God was fine, and nobody saw anything wrong with that. “And without an ephod”: that is the twelve tribes.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: “Afterward”: after those centuries of not knowing, “shall the children of Israel return”, return as Israelites, and that is where we are living right now, “and seek the Lord their God”: we are seeking the Lord our God. “And David their king”: among us is David. Christians can’t explain what David their king means in the last days. “In the latter days” King David is going to be here. We just don’t know who he is. He might be one of your kids.

note.label: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

points: In the black community we were prepared with goals and morals in the home, the church and the school, and the schools were not integrated. One woman said her segregated school was the best school experience of her life, because all her teachers were negro. Her third grade teacher wrote the first book of negro history for children, and her seventh grade teacher wrote a book too. Look how old she is and she still remembers their names.

“For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image”. Image is crucial to us as a community, and our enemy understood that. Integration destroyed that image. She saw people like her in positions, an image to look at that said she was not just nothing.

There is nothing wrong with wanting teachers and influencers that look like you. It gives you comfort and relatability. Do not let the other nations call you a separatist for it; they feel comfortable with their own people too. God made every race on earth. And it was a close-knit community: if you misbehaved in school, the teacher stopped by the house on the way home. That is a nation, a family structure that starts in the household and branches out into the schools.
